source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
summary: A chaptered expedition film following Joe and record-holding Sherpa guides from Kathmandu through Lukla and Namche Bazaar to an Everest base-camp area, framed around the question of why Sherpas thrive at altitude. Unlike his narrated portraits, this one is dialogue-driven (dialogue score 1.0, 72% speech coverage): long walk-and-talk scenes with guides on the trail, a gear-shop scene, a seated interview at a high camp and an expert at a museum. The opening 2 minutes is a dense documentary teaser mixing sunrise summits, porters, archival black-and-white expedition footage and soundbites ('Without Sherpa, nobody can climb'). Visual grammar includes on-screen altitude and peak labels, 3D terrain maps, and licensed news/archival clips with visible source bugs. It ends on a helicopter 'surprise' flight to view Everest, a thank-you to the expedition company, and a studio sponsor read.
hook_analysis: Sunrise alpenglow on peaks (0:00, 0:40) under a fact-led VO from 5 s ('This is the summit of Everest...'), pivoting to the reveal statistic '96%... did not reach it alone'. Then a rapid soundbite montage of Sherpas, archival 1950s footage (1:29), a museum expert (1:49) and a genetics claim, closing on 'Today we will try to discover their secret' (1:40). Replay peak at 0:00-0:15; the strongest peak overall is 22:07 at base camp.
narrative_arc: 8 chapters as a linear ascent: Unsung heroes (thesis + tease, 0:00-2:16) -> Journey to Lukla (gear shopping, flight, 2:16-4:48) -> Preparing (porters, history, statues of Tenzing/Hillary, 4:48-8:25) -> Namche Bazaar (helicopter, town, 8:25-11:57) -> Meeting experts (Kami Rita and others on trail, 11:57-16:59) -> Heading to base camp (trek, 16:59-21:05) -> Life at base camp (dome tents, interview, death-zone explainer, 21:05-24:21) -> Reaching the heights (helicopter surprise and Everest view, 24:21-25:43) -> sponsor.
camera_and_composition: Low-angle wide-lens frames of Joe and guides against deep blue sky and snow peaks are the default (12:22-13:31, 20:46); wide-angle selfies on the trail (16:49, 19:47-19:57). Peak hero shots with on-screen name labels (AMA DABLAM 8:54, 21:06). Top-down drone over Namche's horseshoe (9:53-10:03) and over glacier camp (21:26). Seated two-shot interview at camp with Himalaya backdrop (22:45-23:05). Camera moves not observable at storyboard resolution.
color_and_grade: Cool, very saturated: crushed deep-blue skies, cyan-white snow, punchy orange/purple jackets (mean colorfulness 62, the highest of the six). Sunrise/alpenglow orange on summits used as accent (0:40, 16:09). Archival inserts are black-and-white or degraded (1:29, 5:36, 5:56).
sound_and_music: Auto-captions mark [music] 16 times and [laughter] 16 times - banter and laughter are part of the texture. Speech-free runs are short (max ~33 s), e.g. 1:55-2:16 closing the tease, 19:04-19:36 trekking. Ends with sponsor credit to Epidemic Sound in a studio with audio-meter graphics (25:13).
what_to_borrow: Open with a surprising statistic that reframes a familiar subject ('96% did not reach it alone')
Label peaks and altitudes on screen to give the audience a sense of progress on an ascent
Structure a trek as a linear ascent with chapter titles that read as milestones
End on a planned surprise payoff (helicopter to Everest) that the guides reveal on camera
what_to_avoid_copying: Inserting broadcast clips with visible third-party bugs (60 Minutes at 7:35, a news bug at 15:50) without clearance
Showing a pixelated body (23:15) for shock value
Long unvaried walk-and-talk coverage on the trail (12:22-13:41) - many near-identical frames
Engagement bait inside the story ('if this video hits 1 million likes...')
